phaseReason.specNotObserved: The controller has not seen the latest spec yet.
phaseReason.unpausing: Waiting for the controller to resume the rollout.
phaseReason.workloadNotObserved: The controller has not seen the latest spec of the referenced workload yet.
phaseReason.updating: More replicas need to be updated.
phaseReason.becomingAvailable: Updated replicas are still becoming available.
phaseReason.cutoverPending: The active Service has not been switched to the new ReplicaSet yet.
phaseReason.postPromotion: Waiting for the post-promotion analysis or verification.
phaseReason.oldReplicas: Old replicas are still being terminated.
phaseReason.steps: Waiting for all steps to complete.
abortedText: The update was aborted: the stable ReplicaSet serves all traffic until it is retried.
noReplicaSets: No ReplicaSets of this rollout in its namespace.
noAnalysisRuns: No analysis runs of this rollout.
table.name: Name
dialog.promoteText: The rollout leaves its pause and goes on to the next step, as kubectl argo rollouts promote does.
dialog.promoteFullText: The rollout skips its remaining steps, pauses and analysis and makes the new ReplicaSet stable, as kubectl argo rollouts promote --full does.
dialog.abortText: The update stops and all traffic goes back to the stable ReplicaSet, as kubectl argo rollouts abort does. The rollout stays Degraded until it is retried or updated.
dialog.retryText: The aborted update starts again from the first step, as kubectl argo rollouts retry does.
dialog.statusPatch: Sent to the status of the rollout:
dialog.fallbackPatch: If the cluster's Argo Rollouts has no status subresource (v0.9), this is sent to the rollout instead:
dialog.nothing: Nothing to change: the rollout is already fully promoted and not paused.
dialog.changed: The rollout changed while this dialog was open. Check the updated changes and confirm again.
dialog.pauseText: The rollout is paused by hand (spec.paused) and makes no progress until it is resumed or promoted, as kubectl argo rollouts pause does.
dialog.resumeText: The rollout leaves its pause: spec.paused is cleared and its pause conditions are removed, as the plugin's former resume command and Argo CD's resume action do. Paused at a canary pause step, the controller then counts that step as completed and goes on to the next step, as with Promote.
dialog.nothingPause: Nothing to change: the rollout is already paused.
dialog.nothingResume: Nothing to change: the rollout is not paused.
whyNot.promote: Only a paused rollout, or one in the middle of an update, can be promoted; an aborted one is retried first.
whyNot.promoteFull: The rollout is already fully promoted and not paused, or its update was aborted.
whyNot.abort: Only an update that is under way can be aborted.
whyNot.retry: Only an aborted rollout can be retried.
whyNot.pause: The rollout is already paused by hand.
workload.template: An Argo Rollout takes its pod template from this Deployment (spec.workloadRef): the pods run in the Rollout's ReplicaSets.
workload.scaledDown: Its 0 replicas are expected: the controller scales the Deployment down (scaleDown {{scaleDown}}).
workload.scaledByHand: Its 0 replicas are expected: with scaleDown never it was scaled down by hand.
workload.runsBeside: With scaleDown never the controller leaves its replicas as they are: its own pods run beside the Rollout's.
workload.willScaleDown: The controller scales it down once the Rollout's first revision is healthy (scaleDown {{scaleDown}}).
workload.several_one: {{count}} Rollouts take their template from this Deployment.
workload.several_other: {{count}} Rollouts take their template from this Deployment.
workload.stays: Its own pods run beside the Rollout's: with scaleDown {{scaleDown}} the controller scales the Deployment down only while the Rollout's first revision rolls out, so they stay until it is scaled down by hand.
